summary: A Levite mother hides her son, places him in a protected basket among Nile reeds, and receives him back to nurse after Pharaoh’s daughter finds and adopts him. As an adult Moses kills an Egyptian beating a Hebrew, flees a death threat, helps women at a Midianite well, and starts a family there; meanwhile Israel’s groaning reaches God.
whyItMatters: The river intended for boys’ deaths becomes the scene of one child’s survival through several women’s actions. Moses’ flight leaves him far from Egypt just as the closing lines turn the reader toward God’s response to the people’s bondage.

context.author: Exodus names no writer of the finished book, though it depicts Moses writing particular words. Later tradition ascribes the Torah to him; its composition remains debated.
context.audience: Israel is addressed through its story of rescue, covenant, and worship; this chapter names no narrower first audience.
context.date: The book gives a relative story sequence but no secure external year for the events. The dating and formation of its finished text remain debated.
context.setting: The Nile and Pharaoh’s household in Egypt, followed by a Midianite well and Moses’ new household.
context.literaryForm: Rescue and naming story followed by two interventions, exile, marriage, and a concluding divine-hearing scene.

before.text: Pharaoh has ordered newborn Hebrew sons thrown into the Nile; the opening of this chapter follows a family facing that danger.

here.text: The infant survives through his mother, sister, and Pharaoh’s daughter; grown Moses acts against violence, flees, and becomes a foreigner in Midian.

after.text: God’s hearing of Israel’s groaning leads into Moses’ encounter at the burning bush and his commission to return to Egypt.

outline.heading: A hidden child in a river basket
outline.note: A Levite mother protects her son as long as she can, and his sister watches.

outline.heading: Pharaoh’s daughter takes in Moses
outline.note: The princess recognizes a Hebrew child, pays his mother to nurse him, and later names him.

outline.heading: Moses kills and flees
outline.note: He intervenes against an Egyptian’s beating, is challenged by a Hebrew, and escapes Pharaoh.

outline.heading: A Midianite household
outline.note: Moses helps Reuel’s daughters, marries Zipporah, and names Gershom for his foreign residence.

outline.heading: Israel’s cry and God’s response
outline.note: After the king dies, God hears, remembers the ancestral covenant, sees, and understands.

keyVerses.text: She opened it, and saw the child, and behold, the baby cried. She had compassion on him, and said, “This is one of the Hebrews’ children.”
keyVerses.why: Pharaoh’s daughter recognizes the child as Hebrew and responds with compassion.

keyVerses.text: He said, “Who made you a prince and a judge over us? Do you plan to kill me, as you killed the Egyptian?” Moses was afraid, and said, “Surely this thing is known.”
keyVerses.why: The challenge to Moses exposes that his killing is known and helps explain his flight.

keyVerses.text: God heard their groaning, and God remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob.
keyVerses.why: God’s response to bondage is connected explicitly with the covenant made to the ancestors.

questions.question: Why put a baby in the river when Pharaoh has ordered boys thrown there?
questions.answer: His mother has hidden him for three months and can no longer do so. She coats a papyrus basket against water and sets it among reeds while his sister watches, making the river a dangerous but deliberate place of concealment.

questions.question: Who acts to keep Moses alive?
questions.answer: His mother hides and nurses him; his sister watches and suggests a Hebrew nurse; Pharaoh’s daughter recognizes him as Hebrew, has compassion, and takes him in. The rescue depends on women acting across the boundary created by Pharaoh’s order.

questions.question: Why is the child called Moses?
questions.answer: Pharaoh’s daughter names him and explains the name by saying she drew him from the water. The chapter gives that explanation within her speech without requiring an extra linguistic account to understand the scene.

questions.question: Does Moses’ killing of the Egyptian receive an explicit approval?
questions.answer: The narrator says an Egyptian was striking a Hebrew and that Moses looked around, killed him, and hid the body. The following confrontation and Pharaoh’s threat show consequences, but this chapter offers no direct divine verdict on the killing.

questions.question: Why does Moses flee Egypt?
questions.answer: A Hebrew asks whether Moses intends to kill him too, revealing that the earlier killing is known. Pharaoh then seeks Moses’ death, and Moses escapes to Midian.

questions.question: How does the well scene differ from the conflict in Egypt?
questions.answer: Moses again intervenes when shepherds drive women away, this time protecting Reuel’s daughters and watering their flock. Their father invites the stranger in, and Moses settles, marries, and has a son.

questions.question: What does Gershom’s name mark for Moses?
questions.answer: Moses links the name to living as a foreigner in a foreign land. It makes his displacement audible within the household he establishes in Midian.

questions.question: What does it mean that God “remembered” the covenant?
questions.answer: The text pairs remembering with hearing the people’s groaning, seeing them, and understanding their bondage. It introduces God’s coming action by recalling promises to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, rather than saying the people’s suffering had been unknown until then.

glossary.def: The water-protected container in which Moses’ mother places him among Nile reeds.
The land where Moses settles after fleeing Egypt and where he joins Reuel’s household.
The son Moses names while speaking of his own foreign residence.
